transcript: Last night, I saw Our Class presented at Classic Stage Company. I unfortunately missed its acclaimed New York premiere at BAM earlier in the year so I was really glad to see it getting another run this fall. It’s a three hour heartbreaker of a play telling the true story of a group of classmates in Poland. Five are Catholic and five are Jewish, and with the story starting in 1937, it's evident early on that the characters are going to have vastly different fates. This is a very dark piece, with direct and detailed accounts of the horrors inflicted on the characters and the hundreds of Jewish people during a 1941 massacre in a small Polish village. It took me a bit to get into the play — the textual density combined with how busy and occasionally distracting the staging is was at first off putting to me, but my appreciation for the bold and inventive directorial choices grew over time and the story and performances definitely moved me. So overall, though I had some mixed feelings on the execution and direction, I found it affecting and undeniably impressive. Our Class is running through November 3rd at Classic Stage Company. With that, another program for my collection.
